The engagement ends. The evidence stays.

Sphyr asks each engagement team about your consultants and keeps every answer.

See the 2-minute walkthrough

What goes wrong when the team has moved on

A partner asks you for the file on a senior consultant. The partner has worked with that consultant for three weeks this year. You open the file and find two short project-end forms and a client email someone forwarded. The managing partner has asked you to make this year go better than the last, and this is all you have to send.

The one who presented gets the credit
The consultant who walked the client through the findings gets the credit, including for the model a colleague built the night before.
The last engagement counts for the most
Whoever rates a consultant mostly remembers the latest engagement. The three before it had other managers, and those managers are busy on new clients.
The forms never come back
Engagement managers move straight to the next client, and some never fill in the project-end form. One engagement manager has left the firm, so those forms will never arrive.
A quiet consultant leaves
A strong consultant who rarely presents is passed over and resigns. In the exit interview, the consultant says the partner who did the rating saw one engagement out of four.
Today

The file is one partner's memory of the last engagement.

With Sphyr

The file holds the view of the people who worked with the consultant across the year, collected every two weeks while each team was still together.

Two minutes every two weeks

Sphyr asks for feedback while the team is still together. Every two weeks, each person gets a short card for everyone they worked with, and the whole set takes about two minutes. On each card, the person filling it in chooses how working with that colleague went and what stood out. A note is optional.

Your firm's values on every card

The tags come from a list your head of talent sets up for the whole firm. Every team starts from that list and can add a few tags of its own.

Who gets a say

Each consultant picks a circle of close colleagues: the engagement manager and the rest of the team.

From the second cycle, a consultant can also invite a client lead by email, with the partner's agreement.

Partners decide with the whole year of work in front of them.

For consultants

You see how your work is landing while you can still do something about it.

For partners and engagement managers

You see how the team is doing while the engagement is still running. The decisions stay with the partners.

Most of a rating comes from the person giving it

62% and 53%

of the differences in performance ratings came from who was doing the rating, in two large data sets. Actual performance accounted for 21% and 25%.

Gallup, across industries worldwide.

What Sphyr does not do

Sphyr hands partners a record and leaves the decision with them. The feedback in that record comes only from what colleagues chose to say on their cards, and Sphyr logs no hours or screen activity. No AI writes or scores anything. Your people come in from a spreadsheet, and Sphyr sits beside your HR system.

What stays private

Ratings are pooled, and the person rated sees comments without names.

Who sees what I write?
The person you wrote about sees your note without your name, and ratings are pooled before anyone looks at them. Managers approve requests to edit feedback that has already been sent, so they can see who asked to edit feedback about whom.
What if I didn't work with someone this fortnight?
Choose "No interaction" and move on.
Can clients rate me?
Only if you invite them, with your partner's agreement. Clients can join from the second cycle.
What if I miss a cycle?
The next one opens two weeks later. Your Insights page notes the missed cycle, and that's all.

What Sphyr costs

Sphyr, everything included
₹149per employee per month, billed yearly, plus GST

The rate is the same for every employee and every firm size.

What you get

  • A card every two weeks, about two minutes in all, for the colleagues each person worked with.
  • A record for each person built from those cards, with ratings pooled and comments shown without names.
  • Your firm's own values on the cards, plus team and company OKRs.
  • Each person's view of their own record, and manager views of team and member trends.
  • People imported from a spreadsheet.
  • Setup and training by our team, with support included.
  • New joiners billed from the month they join.

What every pilot measures

Your firm agrees the targets before the pilot starts.

  • How many people take part in each cycle.
  • How many different people give feedback to each consultant.
  • Whether partners found something new in the records, and whether it changed any discussion.
  • Whether consultants found their own record useful, and whether they would keep going.

Results stay with your firm unless you agree to share them.

How we set the price

The pilot fee covers what a pilot costs us to run: roughly 30 hours of our team's time, from setup to the scorecard report at the end, plus the running costs for 12 weeks. At the plan rate, 40 people for those 12 weeks would come to about ₹16,500, about ₹9,500 less than that cost, so the pilot has its own fee.

The ₹149 rate sits above what it costs us to serve each person, and below the value we estimate for a firm even in our most cautious case. By our middle estimate, losing a consultant costs a firm about ₹8.6 lakh in recruiter fees and the months before a replacement is up to speed. Sphyr for 150 people costs ₹2.68 lakh a year, so keeping one consultant pays for about three years of it. The ₹8.6 lakh is our estimate of what an exit costs. Nobody has measured whether Sphyr prevents exits.

What happens after you sign

Your first cards go out on a date you agree with us. Here is what each person gets, and when.

Before the first cycle
In a short kickoff with our team, your head of talent adds the firm's own values, and those words become the tags on every card. Together you pick the day the first cycle opens.
Also before it opens
We show your partners a sample record built from people on four engagements, then the same screen for their own practice, still empty. It starts filling from the date you picked, and the decisions stay with them.
The week before
The managing partner sends each consultant a note. Each consultant then adds the people they work with closely to their circle.
The first cycle
One card per person in your circle, about two minutes in all. While you fill in theirs, they are filling in yours.
After a few cycles
Consultants start to see what their colleagues noticed, along with the notes written to them. Engagement managers see how the current team is landing while the work is still going on, and your head of talent sees who took part, team by team, without chasing anyone.
Every two weeks after that
A new set of cards. Over time each person builds up a line showing how their work is landing.

Careers should be earned in front of the people who saw the work.
